title: SMYRNA
tickerText: SMYRNA, TENNESSEE IS A VIBRANT CITY JUST SOUTH OF NASHVILLE WITH A POPULATION OF 48,000 RESIDENTS. IT HAS PLENTY TO OFFER ITS CITIZENS - FROM OUTDOOR ACTIVITIES AT THE NEARBY EDGAR EVINS STATE PARK TO SHOPPING, DINING AND ENTERTAINMENT OPTIONS IN DOWNTOWN SMYRNA. THE CITY ALSO OFFERS GREAT EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES FOR FAMILIES WITH TOP-RATED SCHOOLS AND UNIVERSITIES. OTHER ATTRACTIONS INCLUDE AN ARRAY OF CULTURAL SITES LIKE THE HISTORICAL SAM DAVIS HOME AND GROUNDS AND VARIOUS MUSEUMS. WITH ITS CLOSE PROXIMITY TO MANY URBAN AMENITIES, AS WELL AS A STRONG SENSE OF COMMUNITY SPIRIT, SMYRNA IS DEFINITELY AN IDEAL PLACE TO CALL HOME! VERY LARGE METRO AREA SET IN THE ROLLING HILLS AND RIVERS OF THE SOUTHEAST REGION. PRIMARY INDUSTRIES INCLUDE HEALTHCARE AND MUSIC INDUSTRY. - LOCATED IN CENTRAL TENNESSEE, 180 MILES WEST OF KNOXVILLE AND 200 MILES SOUTH OF LOUISVILLE, KENTUCKY.

videos.title: Tennessee Rehabilitation Center in Smyrna closes due to federal government shutdown
videos.description:
SMYRNA, Tenn. (WZTV) — The Tennessee Rehabilitation Center (TRC) in Smyrna, a state-run school that helps adults with disabilities learn job and life skills, is shutting its doors as the federal government shutdown cuts off its funding.

Families tell FOX 17 News they were given just hours to pack up and move out, with no clear idea when they’ll be allowed to return.

“It should never have happened, it’s not right that the children are the ones suffering for politicians playing,” said Lori Clements, who drove from Memphis to pick up her autistic grandson.

TRC Smyrna is one of only eight comprehensive rehabilitation training facilities in the country. It serves about 200 adult students, offering hands-on training in auto mechanics, food service, and business. For many, it’s a crucial step toward independence.

But on Friday, parents arrived to chaos. Students were told to vacate dorms, pack up their belongings, even if it meant using garbage bags, and leave campus by Saturday.

“Some of the kids didn’t understand what was happening,” said one parent who asked to remain anonymous. “They were crying. They were upset.”

In a statement to FOX 17 News, the Tennessee Department of Human Services (DHS) confirmed that in-person instruction will close starting Monday. DHS says the agency is working to offer virtual lessons in the meantime, but did not specify when the center could reopen.

TRC student Lucas Graham told FOX 17 News the closure felt unprecedented.

“Schools haven’t been shut down in Tennessee or any other state like this since COVID in 2020,” he said. “I was just kind of shocked.”

For families like the Clements’, the shutdown has left them uncertain about what comes next.

“This may be their only hope for an education, to get a job,” Clements said. “Now what do they do? Where do they go?”
